PART TWO
When You Need Help Now
CHAPTER 15
Thoughts of Ending My Life
If you have already seriously hurt yourself, taken an overdose,
think you may act on suicidal thoughts now, or cannot keep
yourself safe, call your local emergency number now. Move
away from anything you could use to hurt yourself. Tell a safe
person: "I'm having thoughts of suicide and I need someone with
me." Ask them to help you reach support, or contact a crisis
service directly.
You deserve care, whatever has brought you here. These
thoughts do not make you weak or faithless.
When you can't go on
A psalm writer told God plainly how much he was suffering:
Be merciful to me, O LORD, for I am in distress; my eyes fail
from sorrow, my soul and body as well.
Psalm 31:9, Berean Standard Bible
You can be completely honest with God, even if all you can say is
"I don't want to go on." That is a prayer, and He hears it.

84
Scripture and context
The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite
in spirit.
Psalm 34:18, Berean Standard Bible
This psalm speaks of God's nearness in suffering. Feeling no
comfort right now does not mean you have failed or that you
should face this alone.
Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.
1 Peter 5:7, Berean Standard Bible
Peter invites people under strain to bring their anxiety to God.
You can do that while telling someone plainly what is happening
and accepting care.
Story summary of 1 Kings 19:4–8
Elijah under the tree
Exhausted and afraid, Elijah told God that he did not want to
live. In the story, he received food, water and time to rest before
the journey continued. His distress was met with care. This
account is not a treatment plan: if you are at risk now, seek
urgent help. You do not have to earn that help by feeling
stronger or praying differently.
If someone you care about is thinking about suicide
Ask directly and calmly whether they are thinking about
suicide. Listen without arguing, blaming or asking for a
promise. If they have already taken an overdose, seriously
injured themselves, or may act now, contact emergency
services. Stay with them if it is safe; if you are apart, try to stay in
contact while arranging local help. Do not put yourself in danger
or handle a weapon. Help them connect with a crisis service or
health professional. You do not have to manage this alone.

85
A prayer
God, I'm so tired. I don't know how to keep going. Please stay with
me right now. Give me the strength to reach out to someone, and
help me get through this hour. Hold on to me when I can't hold on. In
Jesus' name, amen.
A question for when you have support
Who is one person you can reach out to in the next hour?
A verse to return to
Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will
give you rest.
Matthew 11:28, Berean Standard Bible
Read also:
• Living with Depression (p. 58), for reflection alongside ongoing care.
• Hurting Myself (p. 86), if you are also struggling with self-harm.
• When you need help now (p. 12), at the beginning of this book, collects emergency
numbers and brief support information.
